item.title: Destroyed by a 2015 storm, a Virginia refuge beach lot is now moving 2.5 miles north
item.description: Chincoteague National Wildlife Refuge is relocating its beach facilities to a more secure northern position following significant storm damage. This proactive approach not only aims to cut future repair costs but also accommodates the natural shifts of the island. While new parking arrangements will be established, the former site will transition back into its native ecosystem.
item.dc:creator: TOI World Desk

item.title: Bought in 2016, Indiana bishop’s former home with chapel is now listed at $1.28 million
item.description: After nine years of dedication, an Indiana family has lovingly restored a historic home that once served as a Catholic bishop's residence, complete with a private chapel. Purchased at auction in 2016, they meticulously preserved its original features and completed extensive renovations. Now listed for $1.284 million, the family is ready to embark on new adventures and explore the world.
item.dc:creator: TOI Real Estate Desk

item.title: European wild boars escaped a North Carolina hunting ranch in 1912; a century later...
item.description: Invasive European wild boars, originally introduced to the area in 1912, are wreaking havoc within Great Smoky Mountains National Park. To mitigate damage to delicate ecosystems, park management annually removes around 275 of these feral hogs. The boars breed with domestic pigs, creating hybrid species that further disrupt native wildlife. Efforts to control their population involve trapping, shooting, and implementing fencing strategies.

item.title: Young YouTuber Buys NYC Apartment: Eden Masliah mixes savings and inheritance; questions feeling fully proud
item.description: YouTuber Eden Masliah, 21, has purchased a $740,000 two-bedroom N.Y.C. apartment after saving about $250,000 from her content career and using money left by her late father for an investment. Although the purchase marks a major milestone, Masliah admits she struggles to see it as entirely her achievement because of her inheritance. She is now renovating the apartment and hopes to create a timeless space that reflects her personal style.

item.title: At 14, Sheri Lynch got a grey hippo; 40 years later, she had 1,086 items
item.description: Sheri Lynch has achieved Guinness World Records fame for her extraordinary hippo collection, which began with a single plush toy gifted to her in her teenage years. Over the span of more than forty years, she has gathered more than a thousand hippo-themed treasures from various corners of the globe.
item.dc:creator: TOI World Desk

item.title: A British duke sent six Himalayan tahr to New Zealand in 1904; five survived the voyage, and...
item.description: Himalayan tahr were introduced to New Zealand's South Island by British aristocrats in pursuit of sport hunting back in 1904. Quickly multiplying, these creatures turned into an invasive species, wreaking havoc on native alpine ecosystems. Control measures, including government-led aerial shooting, have not proven entirely effective, creating a challenging situation for conservationists and hunters alike. The management of tahr remains an ongoing struggle within New Zealand's wildlife strategy.
item.dc:creator: TOI World Desk

item.title: Amidst the AI data centre backlash, a Missouri farmer is inviting developers to buy his land
item.description: In Missouri, a farmer has taken the unexpected step of inviting data center developers to bid on his land, despite notable local opposition and recent state restrictions. He believes that data centers could revitalize struggling rural economies by creating jobs and generating tax revenue. The farmer also addresses valid concerns about water use and electricity costs, presenting his offer as an opportunity for growth even when local prospects are dim.

item.title: In 1964, a 27-year-old woman bought an abandoned Maine island and lived alone; 22 years later, it became a wildlife sanctuary
item.description: Witch Island, previously inhabited by the infamous Anna Chittenden—referred to as the 'Witch of Wall Street'—has transformed into a wildlife sanctuary. After her brief stay, Jane Sewall took on the responsibility of safeguarding the isle from irresponsible tourists. In 1986, Sewall gifted the island to the Maine Audubon Society, which is now overseen by the Coastal Rivers Conservation Trust.

item.title: What happened to TikTok star Ayesha Gilamana who died at 28? Everything we know as police detain 3 suspects
item.description: Tragedy struck when TikTok sensation Ayesha Gilamana, popularly known as Shamsu Bibi, was shot and killed while driving. Assailants on a motorcycle opened fire, leading to a crash involving her vehicle. Ayesha's younger sister was injured in the wreck and is now receiving treatment. Authorities have arrested three suspects believed to be related to the attackers, as investigations continue to uncover the motive behind this shocking incident.

item.title: In 1943, Franklin Delano Roosevelt gave Springwood and 33 acres to US; estate had 1,500 acres and 500,000 trees
item.description: President Franklin D. Roosevelt generously bequeathed his family's Springwood estate to the government, substantially enhancing the property throughout his life. By planting over 500,000 trees, Roosevelt transformed the surrounding landscape. This pivotal donation secured the lasting preservation of this notable presidential site, which became both America’s first presidential library and a cherished national historic landmark.

item.title: Meet Kanav Jain: Scottish student who built a low-cost autonomous aircraft to deliver medicines to remote communities
item.description: Kanav Jain, a talented Scottish student, has been awarded the prestigious UK Young Engineer of the Year for creating AeroAid, an innovative low-cost autonomous drone aimed at delivering medical supplies. This versatile VTOL quadplane combines the best features of helicopters and airplanes, making it ideal for reaching remote locations. Jain’s mission is to leverage technology for vital humanitarian assistance, reflecting his commitment as a leader in drone technology workshops.

item.title: Between 1969 and 1972, US released a weevil to fight musk thistle; it later attacked native thistles
item.description: A biological control initiative aimed at managing invasive thistles integrated a weevil specifically targeting musk thistle. Unfortunately, this insect extended its reach to native plant species, leading to detrimental effects on local thistles, including an endangered variety that experienced a decline in seed production. This situation underscores the critical importance of careful evaluation in invasive species control programs.
